decisions.title: Ready for your close-up
decisions.situation: Andrea points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

choices.label: Move right up to the lens
Wave at the small person on screen
Turn around at the crucial moment

result.title: Mostly nostril
result.body: Andrea keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

journal.text: I gave Andrea a very close view of my nose.

decisions.title: The two-headed jacket
decisions.situation: You manage to zip two jackets together. They are now one enormous jacket with four sleeves. This may be your greatest invention.

choices.label: Investigate whether a third one would fit
Leave your invention on the floor

result.title: Back to two jackets
result.body: You work out which zip goes where. Both jackets survive the experiment.

journal.text: I worked out how to separate two jackets I had zipped together.

decisions.title: A principled disagreement
decisions.situation: Andrea says shoes are necessary for going outside. You were not consulted during the drafting of this policy.

result.title: Terms accepted
result.body: Both shoes make it onto the correct feet. A surprisingly productive morning.

journal.text: I let Andrea help with my shoes.

decisions.title: Who said that?
decisions.situation: Your voice echoes in a stairwell. Whoever lives in the walls knows the same words as you, but always says them late.

choices.label: Wait for the walls to start

result.title: A late reply
result.body: The walls return most of your hello. You start again before they finish.

journal.text: I discovered an echo and gave it a very long greeting.

decisions.title: The watermelon investigation
decisions.situation: Andrea jokes that swallowing a seed could grow a watermelon in your tummy. You have questions. Several concern the size of your tummy.

choices.label: Demand to know where the leaves go
Draw a plan for your indoor garden
Announce you are growing a fruit salad

result.title: The witness changes their story
result.body: Andrea admits it was a joke and explains what seeds actually need. You ask why they left out the soil problem.

journal.text: I questioned Andrea until they explained a joke about swallowing seeds.

decisions.title: A very loud rehearsal
decisions.situation: The school alarm sounds during a practice evacuation. Giulia asks everyone to leave calmly. Your chair has other ideas about moving quietly.

choices.label: Follow the instructions and leave your things

result.title: All accounted for
result.body: Giulia checks the class at the meeting point. Your bag can wait inside.

journal.text: I followed Giulia’s instructions during a practice evacuation.

decisions.title: The museum has escaped
decisions.situation: You empty your pocket collection onto the table for Andrea. Three stones. A leaf. A slug you thought was another leaf. The slug makes for the edge.

choices.label: Return the slug before it reaches the floor
Claim the slug lives here now

result.title: Please follow the shiny line
result.body: You describe the stones while Andrea catches the slug on a leaf. Your only moving exhibit is removed halfway through the tour.

journal.text: I gave Andrea a museum tour while a slug escaped from my pocket collection.

decisions.title: The bean is not thriving
decisions.situation: The class bean plant is dead. Giulia asks why your progress chart still says “thriving”. You added a smiley face this morning.

choices.label: Write an honest report on its demise
Ask Giulia where you went wrong
Give it an emotional farewell speech

result.title: A useful post-mortem
result.body: You record the dry soil and brown leaves. Giulia gives credit for the observations, rather than your earlier optimism.

journal.text: I corrected my report about a dead classroom bean plant.

decisions.title: A previous version of you
decisions.situation: Andrea finds an old recording of you explaining how rain works. Your theory involves somebody emptying a bath above the clouds.

choices.label: Ask to keep the recording private

result.title: The expert stands corrected
result.body: You laugh at your explanation. Andrea remembers the questions that came after it.

journal.text: I watched an old childhood recording with Andrea.

decisions.title: Your debut single is chemistry
decisions.situation: Alice secretly records you singing chemistry definitions and adds a dance beat. The file is called “Desperate for Zinc”. They want to send it to the class.

choices.label: Demand credit as the anonymous vocalist
Record a completely unnecessary key change

result.title: An extremely limited release
result.body: Alice deletes it while you watch. They call you difficult. You call them a record label with no permission forms.

journal.text: I made Alice delete a secret recording of my chemistry revision song.

decisions.title: At least you know your name
decisions.situation: Your practice exam is going badly. So far, you have written your name and the date. The date is wrong.

choices.label: Hunt for every easy mark first
Take the wreckage to Alice afterwards
Write an apology in the answer box

result.title: A rescue in small pieces
result.body: You collect enough answers to get moving. Even question one looks less hostile on your second visit.

journal.text: I recovered from freezing in a practice exam by answering easier questions first.

decisions.title: Read at 10:42
decisions.situation: Andrea sends “Where are you?” You are somewhere perfectly ordinary, but the fourth message arrives before you finish typing.

result.title: A workable arrangement
result.body: You agree on a check-in time. Andrea admits the silence worried them.

journal.text: I agreed on clearer check-ins with Andrea.

decisions.title: Apparently this was cool
decisions.situation: Andrea plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.

choices.label: Ask what it reminds them of

result.title: Before they were your parent
result.body: The story is better than expected. You learn something new about Andrea.

journal.text: I listened to Andrea’s old music and the story behind it.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, you try a cracker that tastes strongly of cupboard. The demonstrator asks for a glowing testimonial while holding a camera.

choices.label: Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: A reminder that needs reminding
decisions.situation: You find a note you wrote to help remember something important. It says only, “The usual one, but different.”

choices.label: Assume it will make sense later

result.title: Future you gets better information
result.body: You replace the riddle with a useful explanation and keep it somewhere appropriate.

journal.text: I replaced an unhelpful private reminder with a clear one.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: a prolonged low mood and loss of interest. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs €45.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: Not the tabletop version
decisions.situation: At a craft workshop, you pull the tab on a kit labelled “decorative boat”. A full-size inflatable canoe starts filling the room. The tiny instruction sheet says to inflate outdoors.

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
Climb in and ask for paddles
Insist the picture on the box was misleading

result.title: A long public fart
result.body: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

journal.text: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

decisions.title: One missed intention
decisions.situation: You miss a small personal intention and catch yourself declaring the whole effort ruined. The declaration is much larger than the missed step.

choices.label: Ask whether the intention needs adjusting

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?

Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.
